name: nonApi_pruneLogs
description: Nightly log retention. Deletes aged rows, in batches, from LOG.GeneralLog (by clustered idx range resolved once from the Timestamp cutoff, so the delete is a sequential scan rather than a bookmark lookup per row), HC.IntegrationJob (keeping the latest job AND the latest completed job per integration, so a dormant integration never vanishes from the Usage Data monitor) and HC.ClientErrorLog (the on-device diagnostics harvest; no retention at all until 2026-09-02). Runs from the HC_prune_logs Logic App immediately before HC_rebiuld_indexes; no auth. Deliberately NOT one outer transaction — every batch autocommits, which is the point of batching. Inputs are clamped to sane ranges (@RetentionDays ≥ 30, 100 ≤ @BatchSize ≤ 50000, @MaxBatches ≥ 1, 0 ≤ @BatchDelaySeconds ≤ 600). @BatchDelaySeconds is the throttle: dead time between batches lowers the job's average DTU. Writes one LOG.GeneralLog summary row per run and returns one summary rowset. A runtime error is logged to HC.ErrorLog and re-thrown.

parameters.name: RetentionDays
parameters.description: Keep rows newer than this many days. Default 90; values below 30 are raised to 30 (but see code smell: the cutoff is computed BEFORE the clamp).

parameters.name: BatchSize
parameters.description: Rows per DELETE TOP. Default 5000; outside 100..50000 ⇒ 5000.

parameters.name: MaxBatches
parameters.description: Upper bound on batches PER TABLE in one run (default 200, i.e. 1,000,000 rows per table) so one invocation can never run away. < 1 ⇒ 200.

parameters.name: BatchDelaySeconds
parameters.description: Pause between batches (WAITFOR DELAY). Default 0.5; outside 0..600 ⇒ 0.5. Raise it for a big catch-up.

rowsets.name: PruneSummary
rowsets.description: Always exactly one row on success (none when the CATCH re-throws).

columns.name: ElapsedSeconds
columns.description: Wall-clock seconds for the whole run, including the WAITFOR delays.

sideEffects: DELETE TOP (@BatchSize) FROM LOG.GeneralLog WHERE idx <= @maxIdx AND [Timestamp] < @cutoff, repeated up to @MaxBatches times; each batch autocommits.

DELETE TOP (@BatchSize) FROM HC.IntegrationJob WHERE IntegrationJobId <= @maxJobId AND startedAt < @cutoff AND the job is not the latest (or latest completed) for its integration (#KeepJobs), repeated up to @MaxBatches times.
DELETE TOP (@BatchSize) FROM HC.ClientErrorLog WHERE LoggedAt < @cutoff, repeated up to @MaxBatches times.
Inserts one LOG.GeneralLog row (LogSource 'nonApi_pruneLogs') summarising counts, delay and elapsed time.
Creates and drops #KeepJobs. WAITFOR DELAY between batches when @BatchDelaySeconds > 0.
On any runtime error: rolls back if a transaction is open (none is opened here), inserts one HC.ErrorLog row (HcVersion '<unknown>'), then THROWs.

codeSmells.issue: @RetentionDays clamp is applied AFTER @cutoff is computed — the guard does not protect the delete
codeSmells.detail: Line 60 computes @cutoff = DATEADD(DAY, -@RetentionDays, SYSUTCDATETIME()) from the RAW parameter; line 68 then raises @RetentionDays to 30 if lower. The DELETEs use @cutoff, so a call with @RetentionDays = 1 deletes everything older than one day while the summary log line claims 'Pruned to 30d'. Harmless from the Logic App (defaults), but the documented floor is not real. Compute @cutoff after the clamp.

codeSmells.issue: Header says the summary rowset has three columns; it has four
codeSmells.detail: The header comment (lines 20–21) lists GeneralLogDeleted, IntegrationJobDeleted, ClientErrorLogDeleted; the SELECT at lines 180–183 also returns ElapsedSeconds. Documentation only.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
